article.name: Binder
article.summary: Binder is a local-first structured knowledge base for records, configuration, and relations, backed by workspace-local SQLite and hash-linked transactions. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

contact.note: No published email was found in the official pinned README; SECURITY.md is absent at the reviewed revision, and the official project URL redirects to the repository.

who_what.text: The official repository is maintained under the GitHub account mpazik. Its README describes Binder as a headless knowledge base for tools, agents, scripts, and people, distributed as local software and libraries/CLI rather than a hosted service.

architecture.text: The workspace opener resolves an explicit path, BINDER_WORKSPACE, or nearest ancestor marker, then opens workspace-local SQLite. The KnowledgeGraph composes schema-aware entity/config persistence, filtering, relation resolution, and transaction processing.

SQLite stores records, configs, and transactions. Record/config rows contain IDs, UIDs, optional keys, types, JSON field values, transaction IDs, and tags; transaction rows retain record/config changesets, previous/current hash, author, timestamp, and metadata.

Schema is data in the config namespace. Transaction input processing applies config changes before record changes, validates changesets, and hashes each transaction with a prior-hash link before the apply-and-save step.

The README describes Markdown as a navigable view over entities; editor and LSP clients validate and synchronize file changes with the same workspace repository. MCP exposes schema, search, and transaction tools.

behavior.text: MCP transact accepts record and config changesets and calls KnowledgeGraph.update. A typed record creates; key/UID without type addresses an existing record; the tool schema documents $delete for record removal. The response returns transaction ID/hash and affected record/config counts.

Field changes are typed set/clear/list/relation operations. Entity deletion clears populated scalar fields and removes multivalue fields, preserving prior values in the reversible changeset. Rollback applies inverse transactions newest-first and then deletes those transaction rows, so rollback intentionally truncates active history.

Search provides structured field filters, nested relation includes, ordering, and pagination. The code defines a default limit of 50 and compiles $text substring filters over supported text fields. The inspected path does not include embeddings or answer generation; query documentation's similarity/hybrid descriptions do not by themselves verify those paths as implemented.

Workspace selection is the visible storage boundary. The reviewed record schema and search path do not impose an account, agent, tenant, or project identity predicate; no runtime authorization or isolation behavior was tested.

Transaction provenance includes author, created time, previous/current hashes, and optional message/source/channel/tags. The model offers mutation history evidence but the inspected record/MCP contract does not provide general claim-level source citations, evidence links, or confidence/trust labels.

metrics.evidence: Structured filters and text matching are present, but no answer quality or abstention workload was run.
Updates append changesets and rollback reverses recent transactions; no correction probes were adjudicated.
Deletion uses reversible field clears; no post-delete probes or leakage checks were run.
Workspace-local storage is source-visible, but no cross-workspace or cross-principal probes were captured.
Transactions carry mutation provenance, but the inspected tools lack a general claim-to-source citation contract; no outputs were adjudicated.
SQLite reads/writes and a default search limit are visible, but no Binder timing observations were collected.
No model/token/cost path was found in the inspected repository, search, and transaction interfaces.
SQLite schema is visible, but no bytes-per-record or corpus size measurement was made.

limits.text: This is a bounded read-only inspection at the recorded revision. Runtime correctness, search relevance, transaction durability, editor synchronization, failure recovery, throughput, and security boundaries were not exercised.

Rollback removes selected transaction rows after applying inverses; it is not evidence of secure erasure because old content may remain in other copies, backups, exports, or logs. The reviewed interface also exposes workspace selection without principal-scoped authorization.

The README identifies full-text and semantic search as roadmap work. The reviewed filter implementation shows substring matching; similarity/hybrid documentation statements need code-path confirmation beyond the inspected scope.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run for Binder. The project metric definitions, fixture, and initial status record are linked as methodology and separate execution tracking, not Binder observations or results.
